_readme: Proofs that cannot run in the test suite, and the hash of what they proved.
cockpit/tests/proof-staleness.test.ts fails while a recorded hash does not
match the file on disk. It does NOT run the SQL and cannot know whether you
really ran it -- it converts 'remember to run this' into 'the suite asks'.
A stale alarm is not a proof. It is the difference between a note and a control.
To bless after running one: npm run proof:bless <id>
`--all` NEVER first-blesses and never re-stamps an unchanged proof. Both were
added on 18 Sep 2026 after a convenience call replaced ten true dates with
today's and stamped two never-run proofs as proved. The first blessing of a
proof is somebody claiming they ran a new thing, and that claim is always
A proof may also be BLOCKED: recorded, exempt from staleness, and carrying
`runnable_when` -- a path that does not exist yet. The moment it does, the
suite fails and says the proof is now runnable and has never been run, and
`proof:bless` refuses it until then. That covers two kinds of deferred
obligation: a proof that cannot be RUN yet, and a check that cannot be
WRITTEN yet. Both are alarms with a trigger rather than a silence.

proofs.what: The views aggregate, group and join correctly. The RULES are proved separately and automatically in cockpit/tests/consent-resolution.test.ts.
proofs.how: Paste db/tests/0013_consent_view.test.sql into the Supabase SQL editor and run it. It rolls itself back. Expect two NOTICEs and no exception.

proofs.what: The three invariants of the send record and the authorisation freeze, each SEEN to refuse a row it must refuse. Two of the three are check constraints rather than observations, which is only possible because the row precedes the send.
proofs.how: Paste db/tests/0015_sends_constraints.test.sql into the Supabase SQL editor and run it. It rolls itself back. Expect 'ALL SIX CONSTRAINT CASES FIRED', the neighbour accepted, and three freeze notices. Any 'DID NOT FIRE' is a constraint that is not holding.

proofs.what: The freeze inverted from a denylist to an allowlist: outcome columns writable, every other column frozen INCLUDING ones 0015 never mentioned. 0015's version would have allowed campaign_id to be edited after the fact.
proofs.how: Paste db/migrations/0017_sends_attempts_and_allowlist_freeze.sql, then run its verify block inside begin/rollback. Expect: attempts/last_attempt_at/last_error writable; gate_decided_at refused BY NAME; campaign_id refused (0015 would have allowed it).

proofs.what: A halted run must say why, and an evaluated run's counts must add up: target = excluded + permitted + refused. A shape that does not add up is not a record.
proofs.how: Paste db/migrations/0018_campaign_runs.sql, then its verify block inside begin/rollback. Expect halted_states_its_reason to refuse a halt with no reason; forecast_adds_up to refuse 23+20+200 against a target of 300 and to ACCEPT 23+20+257.

proofs.what: The `unresolved` status is accepted where 0015 would have refused it, the freeze still holds on a row in that state, and the two reconciliation indexes exist.
proofs.how: Paste db/migrations/0019_sends_unresolved.sql, then its verify block inside begin/rollback. Expect the unresolved insert to succeed, gate_basis refused by name, reconciled_at/last_error writable, and 2 index rows.

proofs.what: Variable contiguity refused, an approved row without its approval id refused, the body frozen while status stays writable, and a send naming a non-existent approval refused by the new foreign key.
proofs.how: Paste db/migrations/0020_message_templates.sql, then its verify block inside begin/rollback. Expect: contiguity function t/f/t; variables_are_contiguous fires; approved_has_its_approval fires; status update succeeds then body update refused BY NAME; sends_template_approval_fk refuses HX_NOT_REAL.

proofs.what: clients.whatsapp_sender_sid exists and its shape is enforced (XE + 32 hex). Without this column the quality halt cannot read the number it exists to watch.
proofs.how: Paste db/migrations/0021_clients_sender_sid.sql, then its verify block inside begin/rollback. Expect 'not-a-sid' refused by clients_sender_sid_shape and a well-formed XE… accepted.

proofs.what: sends.campaign_run_id exists and its foreign key refuses a run that does not exist. Without it, a run's refusal rows are not attributable to the run, and a second run of the same campaign would read the first's rows as its own.
proofs.how: Paste db/migrations/0022_sends_campaign_run_id.sql, then its verify block inside begin/rollback. Expect the column to exist and an invented campaign_run_id to be refused by the foreign key.

proofs.what: Attribution is a three-state fact: a campaign attribution must name its send, an organic one must name nothing, and — the one that matters — an insert omitting the column entirely (which the live workflow does) inherits `unknown`, the LOUD state, rather than `organic`.
proofs.how: Paste db/migrations/0023_messages_attribution.sql, then its verify block inside begin/rollback. Expect existing rows all 'unknown'; campaign-without-send refused; organic-with-run refused; and an insert omitting attribution_state to SUCCEED returning 'unknown'.

proofs.what: A `declared` event without declared_by is refused; one with it is accepted; and every other kind is untouched — an objection has no declarer, and requiring one would make a contact's own opt-out unrecordable.
proofs.how: Paste db/migrations/0024_declaration_author.sql, then its verify block inside begin/rollback. Expect: declaration without author REFUSED, with author accepted, and an objection with no declared_by accepted.

proofs.what: The two CHECKs that keep a computed match and a chosen one apart, the PARTIAL UNIQUE INDEX (one current row per lead x listing), and the FREEZE (a notified match resists an edit and permits an outcome). The last two need a row that EXISTS and is then changed, which no constraint-only check can reach. Includes the permitted neighbours: a legitimate computed row, a successor once the first is history, and an outcome written after notification -- a table that refused everything would pass every refusal case identically.
proofs.how: Paste db/tests/0025_listing_matches.test.sql into the Supabase SQL editor and run it. It rolls itself back. Expect 'ALL SEVEN REFUSAL CASES FIRED, and all six permitted cases were accepted'. Any 'DID NOT FIRE' is a guard that is not holding; a MISSING ok on a permitted case is the opposite failure and matters just as much.

proofs.what: An unknown kind is refused rather than stored and never matched (0009's `availabe` in a new place), and an agent's assertion about a lead carries both their words and their name. With the neighbours: a complete agent row, a derived row that needs no author, and area holding a LIST of alternatives in ONE row -- which is lesson 7c, since two rows of an alternatives kind are an AND and match nothing anywhere.
proofs.how: Paste db/tests/0026_lead_requirements.test.sql into the Supabase SQL editor and run it. It rolls itself back. Expect 'ALL THREE REFUSAL CASES FIRED, and all three permitted cases were accepted'.

proofs.what: THE RULE THAT MATTERS MOST IN 0026, AND IT IS NOT A CONSTRAINT. A recompute deletes by source -- field, conversation, note -- and never touches source='agent'. The agent's answer to 'why them?' exists nowhere else and is the only way a name-and-phone list acquires structure. The obvious 'delete every row for this lead and reinsert' destroys it AND LOOKS LIKE IT WORKED, because every derived row comes back.
proofs.how: Given one 'agent' row and three derived rows for a lead, run the recompute and assert the agent row is still present AND carries its ORIGINAL id -- a delete-and-reinsert that happened to write an equivalent row is the same defect with a new primary key. Cannot be run yet: the matching run does not exist.

blocked.reason: The recompute lives in the caller, and the matching run has not been built. There is nothing to run this against.

discharged.note: The rule became provable in the suite rather than in a SQL editor, because the caller was built as a PURE PLANNER: planRecompute() is the only thing that produces ids to delete, so the store applies a plan by id and a delete scoped to the lead cannot be written. Three tests: every derived row is deleted and no agent row; the agent row keeps its ORIGINAL id (a delete-and-reinsert is the same defect with a new primary key); and a lead with only derived rows is fully replaced, so the rule is not 'delete nothing'.

proofs.what: agent_dismissed_lead is a working preference held by an agent, NOT an objection. An objection is permanent, belongs to the contact, lives in the consent ledger, and is recorded because a person asked for it. If the two ever merge, an agent's convenience becomes a permanent legal state on somebody who never asked for it -- invisibly, because both produce the same silence. 0025's header names three safeguards and a migration can only carry two; this is the third.
proofs.how: A source-level boundary check of the kind tests/one-sender.test.ts already does for the provider credential: the gate and its reads -- gate.ts, gate-read.ts, suppression.ts, the consent resolution -- must not import or query listing_matches, and the check must name the offending path rather than return a count. The CANDIDATE-SET query is the one place that SHOULD read it, so the check is a boundary and not a ban. Cannot be written yet: the matching run does not exist, so there is no caller to bound.

blocked.reason: The matching run has not been built, so there is no read path to bound. Recorded now because an obligation recorded and never discharged is worse than one nobody wrote down -- the record proves you knew.

discharged.note: A source-level boundary in both directions: nothing on the gate path reads listing_matches or agent_dismissed, and the matching run does not consult the gate, the ledger or the suppression list. Plus the two tests that stop it becoming vacuous -- every listed file must exist, and the matching side must still read listing_matches, so the boundary cannot be 'fixed' into a ban that blinds the candidate set.

proofs.what: A rating with no expiry date is refused (one we cannot date is one we cannot defend), and an exemption without an author or a basis is refused — because an exemption that is a blank cheque is the door everything walks through and the obligation loses all practical effect. With the neighbours: the same rating WITH a date is accepted, and a complete declaration is accepted. A table that refused everything would pass both refusals identically.
proofs.how: Paste the VERIFY block at the foot of db/migrations/0028_energy_certificate_and_ami.sql into the Supabase SQL editor, inside begin/rollback. Expect: energy_class without a date refused by name; with a date accepted; an exemption missing `basis` refused by name; a complete exemption accepted. Roll it all back.

proofs.what: The stale description of Automation 04 is corrected, and the OTHER FOUR are untouched. A description is what somebody reads when they arrive and want to know what an automation is for; a stale one is how the wrong thing gets built two years from now by somebody who trusted the row. The second half matters as much: an UPDATE whose WHERE clause matched everything would look identical in the first check.
proofs.how: Run 0027, then `select key, left(description,40) from public.automations order by key` and confirm listing_launch carries the new text and the other four are unchanged.
